messages.author: f5bec70b36df06aa
messages.subject: Change font of graph
parts:
Hi @all

A rather simple task, at least I thought, developed into a half-day
search on the internet for some help without any success. I simply
would like to change the font of my ggplot graph to CMU Serif but I
couldn't find a simple way to do it, actually, no way to do it.

Is there a simple way?

Thanks for any help.

Martin

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Change font of graph
parts:
Hi Martin:

If you're using LaTeX and inserting the graph in a document with that
font, then your best bet is probably to use the tikzDevice package.
This post: http://www.macfreek.nl/memory/Fonts_in_LaTeX shows how to
load the font in question in both LaTeX and Xe(La)TeX. I haven't used
tikzDevice myself, but several folks on this list have and may be able
to post an example or two. The idea behind the tikzDevice package is
to render text in R graphs using the same font as the standard text in
a LaTeX document.

Another attractive option if you are inserting the graph in a document
is the knitr package, which is quickly becoming a viable alternative
to Sweave. knitr supports approximately 20 graphics devices, including
tikz; the primary knitr manual has an example that uses the tikz
graphics device, using the tikzDevice package in the background. See
http://yihui.name/knitr/demos and click the manual link toward the
bottom of the page to get started.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Change font of graph
parts:
It is possible to use different fonts in your graphs, but support varies across output devices. I don't think there's a straightforward way to use fonts other than those R has built-in support for, and even those don't always work on all devices.

This may be helpful:
http://wiki.stdout.org/rcookbook/Graphs/Fonts/

Also, take a look at ?pdfFonts.

-Winston

messages.author: d3aaa07872b9962c
messages.subject: Re: Change font of graph
parts:
If PDF works for you, the solution is fairly straight-forward.

Using Computer Modern Fonts in R Graphics by Paul Murrell
http://www.stat.auckland.ac.nz/~paul/R/CM/CMR.html

And if you need PNG or JPG, you can easily convert to those from PDF using poppler or xpdf or whatever.
